title: The theory of gravitation
subtitle: Newton, 1687
subject: sciences
description: In 1687, Newton published a simple and immense idea: the same force causes an apple to fall and the Moon to rotate. Here's what that changes.

hero.hook: An apple, the Moon, the planets: a single force to explain everything.

blocks.text: Before Newton, we already knew a lot about the planets thanks to **Galileo**, an Italian physicist from the 17th century, and , an astronomer who described elliptical orbits. But a clear connection between what falls on Earth and what spins in the sky was missing. **[[Johannes Kepler]]**

In **1687**, **Isaac Newton** published the **, the *Principia*, the founding work of classical physics. He asserts that gravitation is **universal**: it acts everywhere, in the same way. [[Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica]]

Kepler had described the orbits of the planets with precise laws: orbits in **ellipse**, equal swept areas in equal time. Galileo had studied the fall of bodies. But why do the planets stay on their trajectory? What “pulls” them?

Newton answers: a **gravitational attraction**, a force that pulls two masses toward each other. The Earth attracts the Moon. The Sun attracts the Earth. And you also attract a little bit of the Earth... even if it's tiny.

blocks.caption: The story of the apple is above all a story. The idea is real.

blocks.text: Two bodies attract each other with a force which increases with their **mass**, the quantity of matter, and decreases as they move away. More precisely: the force weakens with the **square of the distance**. Doubling the distance divides the attraction by four. The further away you are, the faster the attraction weakens.

blocks.caption: The planets are constantly “falling” towards the Sun… and missing it: this is the orbit.

blocks.text: The Moon is constantly “falling” toward Earth. Since it also has high lateral speed, it spins around instead of crashing.
Newton also gives three **laws of motion**. In summary: an object keeps its speed if there is no force, the principle of **inertia**; a force changes the speed; every action has an opposite reaction.
With this, we can calculate trajectories, **tides**, the rises and descents of the oceans under the effect of the Moon and the Sun, and the orbits. Physics becomes a prediction tool.

sections.title: Powerful… but not the last word

blocks.text: Two centuries later,  corrected Newton for extreme cases, very high speeds and very high gravity, with the . Gravity then becomes a curvature of space-time, and no longer an invisible force. But for launching a rocket or understanding the tides, Newton remains excellent. **[[Albert Einstein]]** [[Relativistic gravitation (Einstein)]]
Newton unifies heaven and Earth: gravitation attracts masses everywhere. It is one of the greatest scientific syntheses in history.
